goal: Stop spending GitHub Actions minutes on private repos: run their CI on the Mac and report the result on the PR.
changed: New bstack skill local-ci: local_ci.py runs a repo's scripts/ci at a commit in a throwaway worktree and posts the `local-ci` commit status; a red run on a PR leaves one comment with the end of the log.
install sets up a launchd agent that ticks every five minutes over open PR heads and the default branch head, skipping any sha with a finished status and rerunning a stale pending one.

claims.claim: Pass, fail with one edited comment, run's exit code following an existing verdict and waiting for a running tick, finished vs stale pending, missing scripts/ci, timeout, moved head, fork PRs, --force and an untouched clone behave as the SKILL.md says.
claims.check: tests/test_local_ci.py, 15 end-to-end tests against a real bare repo and a stub gh; four mutants (skip logic, fork filter, moved-head check, run not waiting for the lock) each turn one test red
claims.remaining: The stub gh, not GitHub. macOS only for install.

claims.claim: Against real GitHub, run --pr posts success on a passing PR and failure plus a comment naming the broken file on a failing one, and the installed launchd agent's first tick gave every open PR head and default branch head a verdict.
claims.check: four private-repo PRs and one throwaway PR with a planted formatting error, statuses read back with gh api; local_ci.py status after the first tick
claims.remaining: The repos are private, so the statuses are not linked here. Only one machine has run it.

next.item: Book local runs' test records in the quality books
next.why_now: Repos that move to local-ci stop producing the Actions artifacts that quality.py fetch reads.
next.impact: Until then those repos' per-test time and flakes drop out of the weekly brief.
